IT & INFORMATION SECURITY POLICIES
Enterprise Password, Access Control & Credential
Security Policy
Complexity Rules, MFA Mandates, JIT Access, and Account Compromise Protocols
Classification: Confidential
Version: 4.0
Owner: Information Security
Standard: NIST SP 800-63B / SOC 2
1. Purpose and Regulatory Framework
This policy defines mandatory requirements for password security, multi-factor authentication (MFA), role-based access
control (RBAC), and credential compromise handling across Apex Global Technologies. This policy is aligned with NIST
Special Publication 800-63B (Digital Identity Guidelines) and SOC 2 Type II trust services criteria.
2. Password Complexity and Passphrase Standards
Minimum Length: All standard employee accounts must use passwords of at least 14 characters. Privileged
administrative accounts (AWS root/IAM admin, database DBA, Kubernetes cluster-admin) require at least 16
characters.
Complexity: Must contain at least one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, one numeric digit, and one special
symbol ( !@#$%^&*()_+-= ). Passwords may not contain common dictionary words, user names, company names, or
predictable numeric sequences.
Passphrase Recommendation: Employees are strongly encouraged to use multi-word passphrases consisting of at
least four randomly chosen words (e.g., correct-horse-battery-staple-2026! ).
Expiration & Rotation Policy: In compliance with NIST SP 800-63B, forced arbitrary 90-day password rotation is
discontinued. Passwords must only be rotated upon suspicion of compromise or when detected in threat intelligence
credential dumps.
3. Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) Requirements
MFA is universally enforced across all corporate systems, including Okta SSO, Google Workspace, GitHub Enterprise,
AWS, and the GlobalProtect VPN:
Approved MFA Methods: Hardware FIDO2/WebAuthn security tokens (YubiKey 5 Series) are the mandatory primary
factor. Software TOTP apps (Okta Verify, Google Authenticator) are authorized secondary fallbacks.
Prohibited MFA Methods: SMS-based and voice-call verification are strictly prohibited due to known SIM-swapping,
SS7 redirection, and interception vulnerabilities.
4. Protocol for Suspected Account Compromise
EMERGENCY ACTION PROTOCOL: What should an employee do if they suspect an account compromise?
If an employee suspects unauthorized access, observes anomalous login alerts, detects altered files, or fears credentials
were entered on a phishing site, they must execute the following immediate four-step protocol:
Isolate Device from Network: Immediately disconnect the device from corporate Wi-Fi or unplug the Ethernet cable,
and disconnect the GlobalProtect VPN. Do NOT power off or reboot the workstation, as volatile memory contains vital
forensic evidence.
Immediate Incident Reporting: Contact the Security Operations Center (SOC) immediately via: 
Emergency Phone Hotline: +1-888-APEX-SEC (+1-888-273-9732, staffed 24/7/365).
Dedicated Slack Channel: #sec-ops-emergency .

SOC Dispatch Email: security-incident@apextech.internal .
Trigger Immediate Session Revocation: From a secondary trusted mobile device, log in to the Okta Self-Service
Security Portal and select "Revoke All Active Sessions & Reset Password", or request an immediate administrative
lock from IT Helpdesk.
Assist Forensics & Preserve Custody: Provide a written timeline of observed anomalies to the Incident Response
Lead and keep the affected workstation locked for IT security collection.
5. Access Control, Least Privilege, and User Reviews
Principle of Least Privilege: Access to production databases, cloud infrastructure, and customer data is denied by
default and granted solely on documented business justification.
Just-in-Time (JIT) Elevation: Administrative access is granted through temporary elevation (AWS IAM Identity
Center / Teleport) with automatic expiration after 4 hours.
Quarterly Access Audits: Department managers must review and re-certify user access permissions every 90 days.
Uncertified access is revoked automatically.
